items.objective: Choose a, an or the correctly before singular nouns.

post.prompt: Complete with a, an or the: "He wants ___ orange."
Complete with a, an or the: "There is a cat on the roof. ___ cat is black."
Complete with a, an or the: "He found ___ envelope under the door."
Complete with a, an or the: "I bought a lamp and a rug. ___ lamp was cheap."

items.objective: Work out the meaning of an unknown or multi-meaning word from the words and sentences around it.

post.prompt: What does "strike" mean here? A) hit with the hand B) hit a ball C) stop working in protest Reply with the letter only.
post.material: The workers decided to strike, so the factory stopped and nobody went to work for a week.

post.prompt: What does "frail" mean here? A) weak and thin B) rich C) angry Reply with the letter only.
post.material: The old man was frail. He needed a stick and a helping arm just to cross the road.

post.prompt: What does "fair" mean here? A) light-haired B) a fun event with rides C) just and equal Reply with the letter only.
post.material: It was a fair game. Both teams had the same chances, and the referee treated everyone the same.

post.prompt: What does "scarce" mean here? A) plentiful B) hard to find C) hot Reply with the letter only.
post.material: Water is scarce in the desert village. People walk for miles to find a little, and every drop is saved.

items.rule: Understanding numbers and prices in dialogues
items.objective: Pick out prices and quantities in a short written dialogue, telling apart pairs such as 13/30 and 15/50.

post.prompt: How much is the ticket? Answer in one or two words.
post.material: A: One ticket, please. B: That is fifteen pounds. A: Fifteen? OK.

post.prompt: How much does the jacket cost today? Answer in one or two words.
post.material: A: The jacket was forty dollars. B: Today it is thirty dollars.

post.prompt: How much is the bag now? Answer in one or two words.
post.material: A: The bag was twenty-five euros. B: Now it is eighteen euros. A: Eighteen? Good.

post.prompt: How many people come to the party? Answer in one or two words.
post.material: A: How many people are coming? B: Seventeen. A: Seventeen? Not seventy? B: No, seventeen.

items.objective: Give the opposite of common adjectives and use opposites in sentences.

post.prompt: What is the opposite of "expensive"? Write one word.
What is the opposite of "cold"? Write one word.
Which word is the opposite of "hot": cold, warm or ice? Write one word.
Which word is the opposite of "cheap": expensive, uncheap or low? Write one word.

items.objective: Choose present perfect for unfinished periods and past simple for finished times.

post.prompt: Complete: "They ___ (visit) Spain in 2015." Write the verb.
Complete: "I ___ (know) my neighbour for ten years." Write the verb phrase.
Complete: "We ___ (arrive) at the hotel two hours ago." Write the verb.
Complete: "They ___ (be) married for thirty years." Write the verb phrase.

items.rule: Must, mustn't and don't have to
items.objective: Choose must, mustn't or don't have to to express obligation, prohibition and lack of necessity.

post.prompt: Complete with a modal: "Visitors ___ touch the paintings." (forbidden)
Complete with a modal: "You ___ bring a pen; the exam office gives you one." (not necessary)
Complete with a modal: "Cyclists ___ ride on the pavement here." (forbidden)
Complete with a modal: "It is a free concert, so you ___ buy a ticket." (not necessary)

items.rule: Identifying the topic of a dialogue
items.objective: Name the general topic of a short written dialogue from key words, without relying on one word alone.

post.prompt: What is the topic: food, travel or health?  Answer in one or two words.
post.material: A: Is breakfast included in the price? B: Yes, and the room has a sea view. A: Good, I would like to book two nights.

post.prompt: What is the topic: weather, work or sport? Answer in one or two words.
post.material: A: The match was cancelled because of the rain. B: Typical. The team trained all week.

post.prompt: What is the topic: shopping, health or travel? Answer in one or two words.
post.material: A: This shirt is too big. Do you have a smaller size? B: Yes, and it is on sale today. A: Good, I will take it.

post.prompt: What is the topic: school, work or weather? Answer in one or two words.
post.material: A: The teacher gave us a lot of homework. B: Yes, and the exam is on Monday. It is cold in the library too.

items.rule: Reading attitude and tone from word choice
items.objective: Infer a speaker's attitude (annoyed, pleased, reluctant, sarcastic, worried) from word choice in a short written dialogue.

post.prompt: How does the man feel: eager, reluctant or angry? Answer in one or two words.
post.material: A: Will you come to the meeting on Saturday? B: Well... I suppose I could, if you really need me.

post.prompt: How does she feel: pleased, sarcastic or shy? Answer in one or two words.
post.material: A: I have to work late again. B: Fantastic. That is the third time this week.

post.prompt: How does the woman feel: eager, reluctant or angry? Answer in one or two words.
post.material: A: Can you help me move house? B: Er... I guess so. If nobody else can.

post.prompt: How does he feel: pleased, sarcastic or shy? Answer in one or two words.
post.material: A: It is raining on our picnic day. B: Lovely weather. Just what we wanted.

items.objective: Work out what a text suggests but does not say, using clues in the text and avoiding guesses that have no support.

post.prompt: How does Dev probably feel about the results? Reply with one word: nervous, proud or bored?
post.material: When the results came, Dev did not open the envelope. He put it in a drawer, picked up his guitar, and played until it was dark.

post.prompt: How did the fans feel about the match? Reply with one word: pleased or disappointed?
post.material: Despite the heavy rain, the stadium was full, and fans sang loudly until the final whistle. Many were still smiling as they left, with wet scarves.

post.prompt: How does Kim probably feel? Reply with one word: relieved, angry or lonely?
post.material: Kim read the message from the hospital twice. Then she sat down, smiled, and let out a long breath. "He is fine," she whispered.

post.prompt: Did Rob enjoy the meal? Reply yes or no.
post.material: Rob thanked the cook politely. He moved the fish around his plate, drank two glasses of water, and asked if there was any bread left.

items.objective: Decide why an author wrote a text (inform, persuade, warn, complain) and what tone it has, using the language the writer chooses.

post.prompt: What is the writer's main purpose? Reply with one word: inform, persuade, warn or complain?
post.material: I have waited three weeks for my refund, and I have called your helpline six times. Nobody has explained the delay. This is unacceptable.

post.prompt: What is the writer's main purpose? Reply with one word: inform, persuade, warn or complain?
post.material: Last Tuesday, the council opened a new library on Mill Street. It has 20,000 books and a children's area, and is open from nine until six.

post.prompt: What is the writer's main purpose? Reply with one word: inform, persuade, warn or complain?
post.material: Our new phone is faster, lighter and cheaper than ever. Buy yours this week and get a free case. You deserve the best.

post.prompt: What is the writer's main purpose? Reply with one word: inform, persuade, warn or complain?
post.material: The soup was cold and the waiter was rude. We asked for a clean fork and waited twenty minutes. I expect an apology and my money back.
